name: 6,7-Epoxymyrcene

papers.title: A Computational Examination of the Uncatalyzed Meinwald Rearrangement of Monoterpene Epoxides

consumer_summary.what_it_is: 6,7-Epoxymyrcene is a monoterpene epoxide, a naturally occurring molecule closely related to myrcene—the earthy, clove-like compound famous in hops and cannabis. Plants create this molecule by adding an oxygen atom to myrcene, slightly altering its chemical shape and how it interacts with the environment.
consumer_summary.found_in: This compound has been identified in the essential oils of blue tansy (Tanacetum annuum), myoga ginger (Zingiber mioga), and wild Sichuan pepper (Zanthoxylum schinifolium).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Right now, 6,7-epoxymyrcene is primarily of interest to structural chemists rather than biologists. Researchers are exploring how this molecule naturally rearranges its chemical bonds under different temperatures, using computational models (Oxford level 5, in silico). Understanding these basic transformations helps scientists map out how plants synthesize complex essential oils and how those oils might change during extraction or storage.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: The only available research on this compound consists of computational chemistry modeling (Oxford level 5); there are currently no biological or clinical studies.

evidence: Measured in 2 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.07–0.08% of total volatiles (0.014–0.016mg per chew).
